newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Astrologer admits error about Venezuelan leader.
newsitem.headline: Astrologer admits error about Venezuelan leader.

text.p: An astrologer who predicted Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera would be forced from office by June 8 admitted on Friday he probably made a mistake.
"Barely 48 hours before the date, I find no visible signs that endorse my prediction," Jose Bernardo Gomez said.
"Everything seems to indicate that Rafael Caldera will overcome the obstacles that hung over his mandate," he wrote in his weekly column published in Economia Hoy newspaper.
At 81, Caldera is Latin America's oldest president and has been dogged by persistent rumours in recent months that his health is failing. His five-year mandate ends in February 1999.

Gomez was briefly detained last October after he predicted that the Venezuelan leader would no longer be in power by June 8. The astrologer said then he would quit his trade if his prediction failed to come true.
He was not available for comment on Friday. His secretary said he was out of town and friends said he was "meditating somewhere in Venezuela...and intensely reflecting upon his own life."
